notes:
1. Emergence of National Leadership — Overview

  • Modern Indian national leadership emerged gradually during the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
  • Early leaders were mainly:
  • Educated professionals.
  • Lawyers.
  • Journalists.
  • Teachers.
  • Social reformers.
  • Businessmen.
  • Later, national leadership expanded to include:
  • Peasants.
  • Workers.
  • Women.
  • Students.
  • Revolutionary nationalists.
  • Socially marginalised communities.
📌 Must-Memorise

Indian National Leadership → Elite Political Awakening → Assertive Nationalism → Mass Nationalism

2. Major Factors Behind Emergence of Leaders

Important factors included:

  • Western education.
  • Growth of press.
  • Modern transport.
  • Political associations.
  • Social reform.
  • Economic criticism of colonialism.
  • Racial discrimination.
  • Historical consciousness.
  • Growth of nationalism.

3. Western Education

  • Western education introduced Indians to ideas of:
  • Liberty.
  • Equality.
  • Democracy.
  • Nationalism.
  • Constitutional government.
  • Educated Indians increasingly questioned colonial rule.

4. English as a Link Language

  • English enabled politically active Indians from different linguistic regions to communicate with one another.
  • It also provided access to European liberal and nationalist ideas.

5. Role of Newspapers

Newspapers helped national leaders:

  • Criticise colonial policies.
  • Educate the public.
  • Spread political ideas.
  • Mobilise supporters.
  • Connect regional struggles.

6. Political Associations

Before the INC, organisations such as:

  • East India Association.
  • Indian Association.
  • Poona Sarvajanik Sabha.
  • Madras Mahajana Sabha.
  • Bombay Presidency Association.

created a generation of political leaders.

7. Social Reform and Political Leadership

Many early national leaders were also social reformers.

They addressed:

  • Caste.
  • Women's education.
  • Widow remarriage.
  • Religious reform.
  • Social equality.

8. Economic Nationalism

  • Colonial economic exploitation became a major subject of nationalist criticism.
  • Economic analysis helped transform political dissatisfaction into a broader nationalist argument.

23. Moderate Leadership — Core Features

Moderate leaders generally relied on:

  • Petitions.
  • Resolutions.
  • Legislative reform.
  • Public meetings.
  • Constitutional pressure.

24. Moderate Contribution

Their major contributions included:

  • Creation of national political vocabulary.
  • Economic criticism of colonialism.
  • Training of political workers.
  • Development of all-India organisation.

25. Limits of Moderate Leadership

Moderate politics was initially concentrated among:

  • Urban educated groups.
  • Professionals.
  • Middle classes.

Mass participation remained limited.
